principles: Reuse the B-ec67 floor executor (enforceAndStampEvidence + runSingleAllowlistedCommand); add no parallel enforcement path.
Ergonomics over validation: the easiest path must be the correct one (a first-class verification_run).
Fail-open at the seatbelt, fail-closed at the floor — the handler is the only load-bearing gate.
Never launder: absent a real pass (exit 0 + selector match on current output), a row must not be covered.
Coordinate additively with B-3b88 on the shared refresh_stale function; never revert its per-row guard.
drivers: The F-045/F-049/F-050/F-061 false-pass family came from hand-authored pass commands; remove the ergonomic on-ramp for that mistake.
A demoted-but-still-passing row currently blocks work until manually re-proven; re-execution keeps it honestly green.
B-3b88 edits the same refresh_stale function in parallel — conflict and silent-revert risk.
The Codex PreToolUse matcher apply_patch|Edit|Write does not match shell execution, so an evidence-pin hook there never fires unless gated on the real token.

options.name: A: verification_run + refresh re-execution + fail-open guard on both hosts, reusing the floor; add-path kept (staged)
pros: No hard break to in-flight callers
cons: Two evidence-write entry points during the staged window
Codex hook correctness depends on an empirical token

options.name: B: only tighten verification_evidence_add to re-run on every add; no new command
cons: Harder to guard a single overloaded command

options.name: C: hard-break verification_evidence_add to consume only a generated receipt id now
cons: Breaks in-flight callers including B-3b88 and other sessions

chosen: A: verification_run + refresh re-execution + fail-open guard on both hosts, reusing the floor; add-path kept (staged)
rationale: A delivers the ergonomic on-ramp and the early-warning seatbelt while leaving the B-ec67 floor untouched and not hard-breaking any in-flight caller; the staged migration de-risks the add-path change; reusing enforceAndStampEvidence avoids a second enforcement surface that could drift from the floor. B is rejected for conflating record-with-run and weakening the on-ramp; C is rejected for an unacceptable mid-program blast radius.

preMortem.scenario: Codex hook never fires because the real emitted shell tool_name differs from our matcher
preMortem.trigger: matcher token guessed wrong (apply_patch|Edit|Write already proven not to match shell)
preMortem.consequence: Codex users get no early teaching message (floor still enforces, so no false pass) but the seatbelt is silently dead
preMortem.mitigation: gate Codex correctness on an e2e that uses the real emitted shell-tool name; ship the Claude Bash-matcher regardless; if the token cannot be confirmed in-env, document the candidate and mark the e2e pending rather than asserting a false green

preMortem.scenario: refresh re-execution collides with B-3b88 editing the same refresh_stale function
preMortem.consequence: one story silently reverts the other guard (double-demote or lost re-exec)
preMortem.mitigation: additive-only edits, re-read the function at DEV time against current HEAD, and a smoke that asserts BOTH the re-execution path and B-3b88 per-row guard coexist

preMortem.scenario: refresh re-execution launders a false pass on drifted material
preMortem.trigger: re-run trusts a too-loose selector or stale command that now passes for the wrong reason
preMortem.consequence: false coverage survives a refresh and re-earns mechanical:true
preMortem.mitigation: re-execution goes through the SAME enforceAndStampEvidence refusal path (selector must appear in current output, exit 0, command matches the pin); on ANY failure or unavailable command leave the row demoted/non-mechanical

preMortem.scenario: fail-open hook masks a real mismatch and creates a false sense of protection
preMortem.trigger: a bug in the hook error path swallows a true deny
preMortem.consequence: operator believes they are guarded when only the floor is
preMortem.mitigation: the hook is explicitly non-load-bearing; a smoke asserts the handler refuses the same mismatch even with the hook bypassed, and the docs state the floor is the handler not the hook
